stories.headline: Samsung guides to record ~$58B Q2 operating profit, overtaking Nvidia on AI-memory boom

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics estimated April-June operating profit at 89.4 trillion won (about $58.44 billion), up roughly 19-fold (1,810.3%) from a year earlier, in preliminary guidance released July 7
key_facts.excerpt: reporting a record 89.4 trillion won ($58.6 billion) for the second quarter... preliminary operating profit for the April-June period surged 1,810.3 percent from a year earlier

key_facts.fact: Revenue jumped 129.3% year-on-year to an all-time high of 171 trillion won
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue jumped 129.3 percent on-year to an all-time high of 171 trillion won

key_facts.fact: The result appears to make Samsung the world's largest quarterly operating profit among major tech companies, overtaking Nvidia, driven by booming demand for AI memory chips
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics appears to have overtaken Nvidia to post the world's largest quarterly operating profit among major tech companies... on booming demand for AI memory chips

key_facts.fact: Analysts estimate the memory business alone generated operating profit in the 90 trillion won range, helped by sharp price increases across DRAM and NAND
key_facts.excerpt: Analysts estimate the memory business alone generated operating profit in the 90 trillion won range, helped by sharp price increases across DRAM and NAND

key_facts.fact: The 89.4 trillion won figure beat an LSEG SmartEstimate, yet Samsung shares slumped on investor worries that AI infrastructure spending may be nearing a peak
key_facts.excerpt: estimated April-June operating profit at 89.4 trillion won ($58.44 billion), beating an LSEG SmartEstimate... shares slump on jitters AI boom may stall

stories.headline: DeepSeek is developing its own inference chip to cut reliance on Nvidia and Huawei, sources say

key_facts.fact: Chinese startup DeepSeek is developing its own AI chip, according to three people familiar with the matter, in a push that could reduce its reliance on Nvidia and Huawei chips
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese startup DeepSeek is developing its own AI chip, according to three people familiar with the matter, a push that could reduce its reliance on Nvidia and Huawei chips

key_facts.fact: The chip is designed for inference -- the stage in which a trained model generates responses -- rather than for training new models
key_facts.excerpt: The chip is designed for inference... rather than for training new models, the sources said

key_facts.fact: The effort remains at an early stage: DeepSeek is reaching out to external partners and holding discussions with chip-design, foundry and memory companies; the effort began about a year ago
key_facts.excerpt: reaching out to external partners and holding discussions with chip-design, foundry and memory companies, the three sources said. The effort began about a year ago

key_facts.fact: A U.S. export ban has helped Huawei gain around half of China's roughly $50 billion domestic AI chip market, though rivals Alibaba and Baidu are also developing their own AI chips
key_facts.excerpt: a U.S. ban on their exports to China has helped Huawei gain around half of the $50 billion domestic AI chip market... rivals Alibaba and Baidu develop their own AI chips

key_facts.fact: The move mirrors global peers: OpenAI last month unveiled Jalapeno, its first custom inference chip developed with Broadcom, while Anthropic has been weighing building its own AI chips
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI last month unveiled Jalapeno, its first custom inference chip, developed with Broadcom, while Anthropic has been weighing building its own AI chips

key_facts.fact: The chip push coincides with DeepSeek's first embrace of outside capital, a planned $7 billion raise valuing it at between $52 billion and $59 billion
key_facts.excerpt: The company was slated to raise $7 billion in a maiden funding round valuing it at between $52 billion and $59 billion

sources.title: China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chip, sources say

stories.headline: Anthropic signs 20-year, ~$19B lease for a 401MW TeraWulf AI data center in Kentucky

key_facts.fact: TeraWulf executed a 20-year lease with Anthropic for a purpose-built AI infrastructure campus, Justified Data, in Hawesville, Kentucky, announced July 6
key_facts.excerpt: The Company has executed a 20-year lease agreement with Anthropic at its Justified Data campus in Hawesville, Kentucky

key_facts.fact: The lease is expected to generate approximately $19 billion of contracted lease revenue over the initial 20-year term, supported by investment-grade credit
key_facts.excerpt: The lease is expected to generate approximately $19 billion of contracted lease revenue over the initial term and is expected to be supported by an investment-grade credit

key_facts.fact: The campus will accommodate about 401 MW of critical IT load, developed in phases, with initial capacity in the second half of 2027 and full 401 MW ramp by early 2028
key_facts.excerpt: The campus will accommodate approximately 401 MW of critical IT load... Initial capacity is expected to be placed into service during the second half of 2027, with the campus ramping to the full 401 MW by early 2028

key_facts.fact: Alongside the Anthropic lease, TeraWulf announced the sale of its 50.1% majority interest in the Abernathy joint venture to Fluidstack
key_facts.excerpt: TeraWulf Announces Anthropic Lease at Justified Data Campus and Sale of Majority Interest in Abernathy Joint Venture to Fluidstack

key_facts.fact: TeraWulf, a former crypto-mining company turned AI infrastructure provider, said the deal establishes a long-duration revenue stream with one of the world's leading AI companies
key_facts.excerpt: TeraWulf, the crypto mining company turned AI infrastructure provider, expects to earn $19 billion in revenue from the agreement

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed Nscale closes $900M revolving credit facility to fund global data-center buildout

key_facts.fact: Nscale announced on July 7 it closed a $900 million revolving credit facility to provide flexible liquidity for its AI data-center buildout across the US, Europe and APAC
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale today announced it closed a $900 million revolving credit facility... providing flexible liquidity to accelerate its AI data center build-out and capital deployment across the US, Europe, and APAC

key_facts.fact: The facility was syndicated across a group of leading banks including J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, MUFG, RBC Capital Markets, Bank of America, Credit Agricole CIB, Deutsche Bank, Mizuho, SMBC, TD Securities and KeyBank
key_facts.excerpt: syndicated across a group of leading financial institutions... This includes J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, MUFG, RBC Capital Markets, Bank of America, Credit Agricole CIB, Deutsche Bank, Mizuho, SMBC, TD Securities, and KeyBank N.A.

key_facts.fact: CEO and founder Josh Payne said the facility reflects institutional confidence in the platform and increases flexibility to build infrastructure that the world's largest tech companies rely on to train and deploy AI
key_facts.excerpt: reflects real institutional confidence in our platform, capital structure, and team... this facility increases our flexibility to do that at speed and at scale

key_facts.fact: Nscale, a full-stack AI cloud platform backed by Nvidia, is a vertically integrated provider combining compute, power and data centers
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale secures $900M for data-center expansion backed by Nvidia

stories.headline: Intel-backed AI chipmaker Syntiant files for a US IPO on Nasdaq

key_facts.fact: Syntiant Corp, a semiconductor and AI-software company focused on 'physical AI', filed for a US IPO on Monday, July 6, filing its S-1 with the SEC
key_facts.excerpt: Syntiant Corp, a semiconductor and AI software company focused on 'physical AI', filed for a U.S. initial public offering on Monday

key_facts.fact: Syntiant posted a net loss of $20.9 million on revenue of $64.5 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, versus a $14.1 million loss on $66.6 million revenue a year earlier
key_facts.excerpt: posted a net loss of $20.9 million on revenue of $64.5 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared with a net loss of $14.1 million on revenue of $66.6 million a year earlier

key_facts.fact: The Irvine, California company, founded in 2017 by CEO Kurt Busch and others, develops low-power AI processors that run machine-learning models directly on devices rather than in the cloud
key_facts.excerpt: Founded in 2017 by semiconductor industry veterans, including CEO Kurt Busch, Syntiant develops low-power AI processors and software that enable devices to perform tasks locally rather than relying on cloud data centers

key_facts.fact: Backers include Intel Capital, Microsoft's M12 and Knowles Corp; the company booked $270 million in revenue for the 12 months ended March 31, 2026 and plans to list on Nasdaq under ticker SYTN in an estimated ~$300 million raise
key_facts.excerpt: booked $270 million in revenue for the 12 months ended March 31, 2026. It plans to list on the Nasdaq under the symbol SYTN... we estimate could be $300 million in an initial public offering

stories.headline: China embodied-AI unicorn Robot Era raises ~$137M led by state-owned Chengtong Fund

key_facts.fact: Tsinghua-born embodied-AI startup Robot Era (Xingdong Jiyuan, also rendered Stardust AI) announced on July 6 a new ~RMB 1 billion (about $137 million) round led by Chengtong Fund, the state-owned capital operation platform under SASAC
key_facts.excerpt: Tsinghua University-backed embodied AI unicorn Stardust AI (Xingdong Jiyuan)... announced a new RMB 1 billion (about $137M) funding round on Monday, led by Chengtong Fund... the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC)

key_facts.fact: The round also drew Jiangxi State-owned Capital Control, Guoyuan Equity, Yufu Sino-Singapore Fund and Hangzhou Capital, plus financial investors including CICC, Ubiquant and Hony Capital
key_facts.excerpt: The round also drew participation from Jiangxi State-owned Capital Control, Guoyuan Equity, Yufu Sino-Singapore Fund, and Hangzhou Capital, together with financial investors CICC Renault, Ubiquant, Hony Capital

key_facts.fact: The capital caps a two-month fundraising sprint totaling RMB 2.5 billion, pushing cumulative 2026 funding above RMB 3.5 billion, one of the fastest raises in China's embodied-AI sector
key_facts.excerpt: total capital raised in just over two months reaches RMB 2.5 billion, and cumulative 2026 funding exceeds RMB 3.5 billion

key_facts.fact: A March 2026 strategic round valued the company above RMB 10 billion and brought in overseas strategic capital including Samsung and Singtel; an April Series B+ raised over $200 million led by SF Group
key_facts.excerpt: In March 2026, Stardust closed a RMB 1 billion strategic round that valued the company above RMB 10 billion and brought in overseas strategic capital including Samsung and Singtel. In April, it closed a USD 200 million... Series B+ round led by SF Group
